significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that a distributed "set signature" encodes membership and cardinality before enumeration, while emitted-member inhibition and premature stopping causally determine which stored members are omitted; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling with form-(ii) causal components, rather than a mere existence claim. It establishes both a phenomenon—individually retrievable members disappear systematically during set serialization—and a mechanism that predicts later omissions from inhibition strength and stopping from decoded cardinality, thereby fixing explanations and interventions for several related failure modes. Geva et al.'s 2023 analysis of factual-recall stages makes the distinction between stored knowledge and failed extraction consequential; the clearly distinguishable negative branch here would rule out a unified latent-set/serialization account, although partial failure of the three subclaims would be less decisive. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic of knowledge representation and retrieval would not earn this score: the specific decomposition into set encoding, sequential inhibition, and cardinality-conditioned stopping is what raises it above the median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "decoded cardinality signal," the "emitted-member suppression removal" intervention, and a "set-cardinality-aware stop calibration," which downstream researchers or white-box deployment engineers could use rather than merely receiving an explanation. These handles are ex ante or online: they act before the model has prematurely stopped or completed an omission, leaving an action window during generation. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—emitting members should suppress remaining-member retrieval signals, while decoded cardinality should forecast stopping—across the broadly asserted class of finite-set queries, although activation access and possible architecture dependence limit uptake outside model researchers and builders. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: a generic investigation of query-dependent knowledge retrieval supplies neither these forward-looking controls nor the claimed transferable inhibition/cardinality relations.
